name: TunnelSnake
iocPatterns: SOCKS proxy usage for outbound and inbound traffic
SSH/RDP tunneling via Plink or ngrok
Data collection stages in local directories before cloud upload
Usage of system32 drivers directory with .dat extensions
keyCapabilities: Stealthy network control via kernel space packet filtering
Bypassing security software using direct system calls
Data exfiltration via public cloud services (Dropbox/OneDrive)
recommendedActions: Block known tunneling tools (ngrok, Chisel, Plink) and their associated high-risk IPs.
Implement advanced EDR rules to flag unauthorized kernel memory access or non-standard IOCTL codes.
Monitor and alert on large amounts of file movements into temporary directories by processes like rundll32.exe.
Scan all web servers for known web shell signatures, specifically China Chopper variants.
Implement SSL/TLS inspection to detect non-standard traffic patterns in encrypted DNS or HTTP streams.
Audit syssetup.dll usage for anomalous execution via the system command processor.
Restrict access to and monitor interaction with public cloud providers (Dropbox, OneDrive) from high-value servers.
Isolate segments containing critical infrastructure management to mitigate risk of local lateral movement.
campaignsText: The TunnelSnake campaign has been active since at least 2018-2019, with its associated actors having records dating back to 2013. It follows a disciplined collection cycle: gaining access via web shells, establishing persistent kernel-level presence with Moriya, and camouflaging C2 traffic through complex tunnel layers until high-value data can be exfiltrated. The repeated use of infrastructure sharing and overlapping tools labels it as a core component of the Chinese espionage apparatus.
description: TunnelSnake is a sophisticated cyber espionage campaign linked to Chinese-affiliated threat actors (TA428/TA416) that utilizes high-stealth kernel-level rootkits and complex protocol tunneling. The group specifically targets government, telecommunications, and infrastructure entities in Asia and Africa to conduct long-term data collection.
goals: TunnelSnake primarily conducts state-sponsored espionage with goals focused on the theft of sensitive information from critical infrastructure and government entities. Their targeting profile is geographically concentrated in Asia (including Vietnam, Malaysia, and Thailand) and Africa, specifically focusing on targets in the telecommunications, energy, defense, and diplomacy sectors.
